title: VibeVoice: Expressive Podcast Generation with Next-Token Diffusion
claim: A single autoregressive model conditions on voice and text inputs and uses a diffusion head to generate long continuous speech, step by step.
layout: Legend top-left, inputs bottom-left, central model bar, repeated autoregressive columns left-to-right
description: A wide system diagram built around a light-blue horizontal bar labeled VibeVoice. Top-left is a legend of tokenizer encoder/decoder trapezoids, a diffusion head box D, a discrete text token circle, and hatched blue (acoustic) and orange (semantic) latent blocks. Bottom-left shows the user input: three cartoon speaker avatars with voice waveforms passing through an acoustic encoder A into blue latent blocks, plus a text script of dialogue lines that becomes a row of circles ending in <Start>. At bottom right, repeated columns take the previous acoustic latent, add a semantic latent from the semantic encoder S, and feed back into the model. Above the bar, repeated columns run D to a latent block to decoder A to a waveform. The columns end with <End> and a 90 min speaker icon. Dotted arrows show the feedback loop.
caption: Scalable and expressive podcast synthesis with VIBEVOICE. Voice prompts and text scripts provide initial input. VIBEVOICE processes hybrid context features, and its hidden states condition a token level Diffusion Head (D), which predicts acoustic VAE for speech segments, subsequently recovered by acoustic decoder (A).
abstract: Generating long-form, multi-speaker conversational audio like podcasts poses significant challenges for traditional Text-to-Speech (TTS) systems, particularly in scalability, speaker consistency, and natural turn-taking. We present VibeVoice , a novel model designed to synthesize expressive, long-form speech with multiple speakers in a zero-shot manner. A core component of our approach is the continuous speech tokenizers operating at an ultra-low frame rate of 7.5. This tokenizer effectively preserves audio fidelity while significantly boosting computational efficiency for processing long sequences. To facilitate training on authentic conversational dynamics, we have developed an annotation pipeline that generates pseudo transcriptions and turn-taking labels for extensive podcast data. Leveraging this data and our efficient tokenizer, VibeVoice employs the next-token diffusion framework. This enables VibeVoice to: (1) synthesize long-form speech (up to 30 minutes) with up to 4 speakers, surpassing the typical 1-2 speaker limits of many prior models; and (2) achieve a high degree of naturalness in turn-taking, pacing, and the rendition of subtle non-lexical cues (such as breaths and lip smacks), which are crucial for listener immersion and capturing the authentic vibe of expressive conversations.
